change: B: RBP_V3_RADIX_AGG (radix path only). 1 = B2, skip score-0 keys in the radix passes and the gather when the range has at least want nonzero documents; 2 = B1 + B2, plus warp-aggregated bucket adds with __match_any_sync. Default 0 = v3-3.
motivation: CPU replay of the laptop dry run (25 calibration queries, W=4096, development): about 48% of a range's documents score 0; in about 97% of ranges the first pass's largest bucket (digit 0, scores < 4096) holds more than half the keys; the modeled same-bucket depth of a warp's bucket atomicAdd is about 30 of 32 lanes in pass 1. Expected gain is small: radix select+gather is about 8% of the pre-merge critical path (laptop development reading).

B2: In the existing max-key loop (only when want < range_docs, i.e. when passes run) every thread also counts its nonzero-score slots; a warp sum (__reduce_add_sync) per warp is stored next to the warp max and summed after the existing barrier, so no extra barrier is added.

skip0 = nonzero >= want. If skip0, the passes count only keys with score != 0 (zero-score slots are skipped before their tie_rank load) and the gather skips them too. If not, the passes and gather are exactly v3-3's.
The max-key loop itself is unchanged (it still visits every slot).
B1: Only with RBP_V3_RADIX_AGG=2, in the passes (not the gather): the slot loop runs warp-uniformly (s0 = warp base, s = s0 + lane, condition on s0), each lane computes its bucket b or 'none' (256), peers = __match_any_sync(full mask, b), and the lowest lane of each group with b != none adds __popc(peers) to buckets[b].
Implemented only after B2 passes its fixtures.

exactness: Keys are unique and a nonzero score always beats a zero score in the key's high bits, so when the range has >= want nonzero documents the want largest keys are all nonzero-score keys: the want-th largest key over the nonzero keys equals the want-th largest over all keys, and the gather (key >= threshold) selects exactly the same keys. Zero-score keys are below that threshold, so skipping them in the gather changes nothing; it only avoids their tie_rank loads.
When nonzero < want the zero-score keys are part of the answer (ties at score 0 decided by tie rank) and skip0 is false: v3-3 behaviour exactly.
Pass termination is unchanged: keys are unique, so the boundary bucket eventually holds exactly the remaining count, or the last digit is reached.
B1 adds the same count to the same bucket (popc of the lanes sharing it), so every bucket total, and hence every boundary, is unchanged.
edge_cases_and_bugs_checked: want == range_docs (k >= range docs): no passes, threshold 0, all keys gathered, zeros included: B never applies (the counting is inside the want < range_docs branch).
nonzero exactly want-1 / want / want+1: fixture v34-nonzero-around-* (k-1, k, k+1 per range, every k, both W). want-1 keeps v3-3 behaviour; want and want+1 skip zeros.
A range where every document scores 0: nonzero = 0 < want, v3-3 path (fixture v34-zero-range).
Ties at the k-th score across the zero/nonzero boundary: fixture v34-zero-boundary-ties-* (k-3 nonzero: k-th is a zero tie, v3-3 path; exactly k nonzero with the smallest scores tied: skip path).

B1: the loop condition must be warp-uniform for __match_any_sync with a full mask; s0 = thread - lane + i*threads is the same for all lanes of a warp, and threads is a multiple of 32 (host check). Out-of-range lanes (s >= range_docs, only in the last iteration) take part with b = none and load nothing.
B1: 'none' = RBP_RADIX_BUCKETS (256) is outside the bucket range, so it never collides with a real digit.
__reduce_add_sync needs sm_80+; builds are sm_89 only.
Static shared memory grows by 128 bytes (per-warp nonzero counts) only when the switch is on; recorded in the resource table.
risks: The extra nonzero count in the max loop costs one compare/add per slot; B2 pays off only if enough zero keys are skipped in the passes (pass 1 counts every slot; the replay says ~48% are zero).

B1: __match_any_sync is not free (it is a multi-cycle instruction); with mostly-distinct buckets in later passes it can cost more than the atomics it saves. The replay says pass 1 is ~30-deep, pass 2 ~14-16, later passes ~1-2.
Skipping zeros helps the range blocks, not the merge, which dominates at k >= 100 (change D).
